answer: In an agent marketplace, the trading network forms a trellis in which each identity is a vertex. Every agent must escrow funds for 30 days, and its share of job-allocation votes is proportional to that stake, not its account count. Stake is the costly signal: creating a thousand identities with the same total deposit buys no extra voting power. To gain influence, an attacker must lock up proportionally more capital and forgo its use elsewhere.
